outcomeNote: Mishna stating rules; no named parties.

segments.he: וְלַד חַטָּאת, וּתְמוּרַת חַטָּאת, וְחַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ – יָמוּתוּ,
segments.en: «MISHNA:» This mishna, which also appears in tractate Temura, deals with the five sin offerings left to die. It is cited here because of its relevance to the halakhot of misuse. The mishna first mentions three of those offerings: «The offspring of a sin offering, and» an animal that is «the substitute for a sin offering,» whether or not the owners achieved atonement by means of another offering, «and a sin offering whose owners have died» before the offering was sacrificed, «shall die.»

segments.he: וְשֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ, וְשֶׁאָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם, אִם מִשֶּׁכִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים – תָּמוּת. וְאֵינָהּ עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה, וְלֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין.
segments.en: «And» the other two sin offerings left to die are the sin offering «whose year» since birth «passed» and is therefore unfit for sacrifice, «and» a sin offering «that was lost and» when it was «found» it was «blemished,» with regard to which the halakhot are as follows: «If» the sin offering was found «after the owner achieved atonement» through the sacrifice of another animal as a sin offering, then the blemished animal «shall die, and it does not render» a non-sacred animal exchanged for it «a substitute,» as it is has neither inherent sanctity, which would make it fit for sacrifice on the altar, nor sanctity that inheres in its value. «And» one «may not derive benefit» from the found animal ab initio, «but» if he derived benefit from the animal he is «not» liable for its «misuse.»

segments.he: וְאִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא כִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים – תִּרְעֶה עַד שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב, וְתִמָּכֵר וְיִקְחוּ בְּדָמֶיהָ אַחֶרֶת. וְעוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, וּמוֹעֲלִין בָּהּ.
segments.en: «And if» the animal whose year passed was found «before the owner achieved atonement,» the found animal «shall graze until it becomes blemished [shetista’ev],» at which point it may not be sacrificed; «and it shall be sold and» the owner «shall purchase another» animal «with» the «money» received from «its» sale. The animal that was found blemished may be sold immediately, and the owner shall purchase another animal with the money received from its sale. In both cases, the animal «renders» a non-sacred animal exchanged for it «a substitute,» and one who derives benefit from it is liable for «misusing it.»

moves.summary: three sin offerings left to die
after atonement: dies, no substitution, no meilah
before atonement: grazes, sold, has meilah

positions.claim: offspring, substitute and sin offering whose owner died are left to die
an overage or lost-and-found blemished sin offering dies if atonement was already achieved (no meilah, no substitution); otherwise it is sold and has meilah
